This robot collided. Choosing a checkpoint to
retrain needs its lineage, sensor contract, and
exact test results. FalkorDB connects that evidence.
My agent used MCP and FalkorDB to
launch real robot training. The run passed
four validation gates.
It chooses a starting checkpoint and calls
start training. The guardrail approves the evidence
and budget before the worker starts.
FalkorDB connects each policy to its training
run, evaluations, failures, and recorded decisions.
Its shortest path query returned a passing
ancestor one hop away. The agent compared
17 eligible origins and chose a different
checkpoint.
The guardrail check sensor contracts, artifact hashes,
complete validation, and the training budget. It
can veto an incompatible origin.
Before training, a decision saves the model,
tool calls, Cypher, parameters, and returned records.
Planning stops without FalkorDB.
The worker trained 61,440 PPO steps, then
reloaded the checkpoint for 180 validation episodes.
All four suites passed the unchanged gate.
Target collisions were three in sixty. Open
had zero. Static and crossing had one
each in 40.
But the parent had two target collisions
and no crossing collisions. Both measures got
worse. Passing the gate does not establish
an improvement, so I kept the demo
policy unchanged.
The next agent read that regression and
the weighted graph ranking. Its context limit
stopped the attempt before training. I did
not retry.
The shipped graph selected checkpoint passed all
four validation suites and fresh confirmation. Eight
target collisions in a 100 episodes below
the 10% limit.
